messages.subject: Problems with the cut files
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

I was using seewave to cut out some undesired parts of my sound files (some seconds at the begging and at the end), but when I save the cut files they are different from the originals.
The new files are correctly cut but it sounds different, and although I couldn't exactly detect the problem, I am guessing it is something with the intensity.
So, as I would use this cut files to run a PSD analysis I think this differences could give me wrong information.
Also, another problem with the new files is that they are not recognizable by Raven, but I can open it with Audacity. So I can see that my script is doing something more to my files than just cut the seconds I asked for, but I still don't know what it is.
Does anybody have a suggestion on what it might be?

I attached an example of the original (example.wav) and the cut file (example.wavfinal.wav), and my code is below.

Thank you!

___________________________________________________

#Finding wave files#

sounds = list.files(path=folder, pattern = ".wav", all.files = TRUE )

nfiles <- length(sounds)

#Reading wave files#

list.file <- list()

for(i in 1:(nfiles))

{list.file[[i]]= readWave(sounds[i]) }

#Cutting the first few seconds#

t0 <- 0

t1 <- 2.12
list.cut <- list()

for(k in 1:(nfiles)) { list.cut[[k]]= deletew(list.file[[k]], from= t0, to=t1, output="Wave")  }

#Cutting the last seconds #

t2 <- 5

t3 <- 7.97
nfiles2 <- length(list.cut)

list.cut2 <- list()

for(m in 1:(nfiles2)) { list.cut2[[m]]= deletew(list.cut [[m]], from= t2, to=t3, output="Wave") }

# Saving  #

for(z in 1:(nfiles2)) { savewav(list.cut2[[z]], filename= paste(sounds[[z]], "final.wav", sep="")) }

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Problems with the cut files
messages.body_plain:
Dear Amanda,

Sorry for the late reply.
The problem probably arises because savewav() rescales by default to a maximum of 2^15 (16 bits).
You then need to use the argument 'rescale', for instance:

# edition
s <- readWave("example.wav")

t0 <- 0
t1 <- 2.12

scut <- deletew(s, from= t0, to=t1, output="Wave")

t2 <- 5
t3 <- 7.97

scut <- deletew(scut, from=t2, to=t3, output="Wave")
# range values
range(s@left)
range(scut@left)
# save as a .wav file
savewav(scut, file="example_wavfinal.wav", rescale=range(scut@left))
## check
res <- readWave("example_wavfinal.wav")
range(res@left)
## oscillo() also rescales to the maximum so that the wave appears 'loud'
oscillo(res)

You can safely compute a PSD on these files.

HTH

Jerome

messages.subject_clean: Sound analysis and synthesis with R: new book
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new Springer book entitled "Sound analysis and synthesis with R" is now available here <https://www.springer.com/fr/book/9783319776453>.

The book does not deal with seewave only but with most packages related to sound.

I tried to explain as much as I could both theory and practice.

Several questions/solutions addressed in the discussion list were included in the book, so thanks to all for your contribution!

Best,

Jerome

messages.subject: >spectro(2018): best R spectrogram contest
messages.body_plain:
-- sorry for cross-posting --

Dear all,

It is my pleasure to announce the contest >spectro(2018), a friendly and informal contest for the best spectrogram generated with R code.

The spectrogram is a 2D/3D key visualisation tool for bioacoustics, ecoacoustics and other sound related disciplines. The spectrogram is not only useful for science, it can also be a nice graphical object with delicate shapes and colours.

The aim of this contest is to share the beautiful sounds, R codes and spectrograms you may have in your files so that it can help others to produce nice graphics and figures.

But overall, the idea is to join science, fun, and maybe the arts!

Here are some information about the organization of the contest:

. deadline : 15  September 2018
. application: a single submission per candidate; send wav sound + R code + png image to jerome...@mnhn.fr with the email title ">spectro(2018)"
. sound: .wav file / no limits, any recording (animal, habitat, voice, music, etc) or synthetic sound built with R
. code: .r file / only within R language, any package but no call to external software, the code should be fully repeatable
. image: static .png file / no limits in the choice of colour and size but should be readable on a web page
. rights: you accept that your material appears on seewave webpage <http://rug.mnhn.fr/seewave/>
. international voting committee: Fanny Rybak (France), Nadia Pieretti (Italy), Susan Fuller (Australia), Stefanie LaZerte (Canada), Tess Gridley (South Africa)
. publication of the results: October-November 2018
. prize: 1 printed sample of the book Sound analysis and synthesis with R <https://www.springer.com/fr/book/9783319776453> for the winner, 1 electronic version of the same book for the second and the third, kindly offered by Springer, Berlin <https://www.springer.com/>

Have fun and good luck!

Jerome
